correctness.rationale: Every retained edge of a cactus cycle is a bridge unless the entire original cycle is retained, since no alternative cycle uses that edge. Hence the independent edge-block factorization is exact. Differentiating gives Cov(X,B)=p(1-p)[m-sum c_j^2 p^(c_j-1)], where the bracket is strictly decreasing for any cycles. Uniform e-subsets give the stated falling-factorial conditional means and nonpositive second differences. Independent exhaustive graph traversal checks 24 complete rational Bernoulli joint laws on eight small cactus examples and eight discrete-concavity sequences. Domain m>=1, 0<p<1, all c_j>=3; endpoints give zero covariance.

value.rationale: The bivariate PGF supplies the complete joint finite-sample law of retained links and failure-critical bridges for every simple cactus geometry, independent of graph size or assembly topology. It yields a sharp, necessary-and-sufficient one-threshold change from positive to negative covariance and a discrete concavity theorem for fixed-budget bond retention. These are natural reliability and redundancy measures, not an arbitrary parameter slice or tiny numerical gain. The simple block proof is stated without overstating breadth.
